Location

How does location impact listing performance?

Visualizing neighborhood performance across Boston...

Interaction: Click on one of the Room Types in the legend above to filter by that room type. Only that room type will be available to see. Click away to get all room types to show.

Takeaways:

  • Downtown and waterfront neighborhoods command premium prices: The darkest-shaded areas on the map reveal that neighborhoods like the North End and Seaport have the highest median prices, likely due to their proximity to major attractions, business districts, and tourist destinations.
  • Outer neighborhoods offer more affordable options: Lighter-shaded areas in neighborhoods like Mattapan, Hyde Park, and West Roxbury show significantly lower average prices, indicating that distance from the city center creates more budget-friendly alternatives for travelers.
  • Review volume doesn't always correlate with price: When hovering over different neighborhoods, you can observe that some high-priced areas have relatively fewer reviews, while more affordable neighborhoods often show higher review counts, suggesting greater booking frequency in budget-friendly locations.
  • Location creates distinct pricing tiers: The map clearly shows three pricing tiers across Boston: premium downtown/waterfront areas, mid-range popular residential neighborhoods (like Jamaica Plain and Allston), and budget-friendly outer neighborhoods, demonstrating that geographic location is a primary driver of pricing strategy.
